subject: Unexplained token surge and VAT split — request for per-endpoint audit
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@fastlaneai.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: Fastlane AI Billing <billing@fastlaneai.com>
Date: 2026-05-10T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: April invoice — unexpected token surge / VAT handling

Hi Avery,

We received the April invoice (invoice #RL-2026-0045) and the total tokens billed are ~3.4M, which is ~11x higher than our expected range (we typically see ~300k/month). Can you provide a per-endpoint breakdown and any insight into what drove the spike?

A few notes that might help: we had a short-lived internal test on 2026-05-04 where we streamed longer contexts to a new prompt variant; the experiment was turned off quickly but it may have generated a lot of tokens. We also saw a flurry of retries from one of our EU workers that morning.

Separately, the invoice shows VAT applied to the full amount. Fastlane AI is a US-headquartered company, but we have an EU subsidiary that handles some customers — can you confirm how you determined VAT applicability here? We need this for our tax team.

Can you send:
- token-by-endpoint (streaming vs non-streaming) for 2026-04-28 to 2026-05-04
- a list of any duplicate request IDs or obvious retry floods
- confirmation of VAT logic used for this invoice

We're putting this invoice on hold until we have the breakdown. FYI I've attached the invoice stub.

Thanks,
Marta Lopez
Head of Revenue Ops
Fastlane AI

Ben/Laura — can you confirm ETA for the logs and a short reconciliation? I will keep Fastlane in the loop and we can set up a quick call if needed.

Subject: VAT application & provisional reconciliation for invoice RL-2026-0045

Hi Marta,

Thanks — quick update from finance while Ben/infra complete the logs:
- Our billing system evaluated VAT based on the billing country on file (we use the billing address and tax ID). At present the invoice is routed as VAT-applicable because the billing contact was set to your EU subsidiary in the tenant metadata.
- If Fastlane provides evidence that the paying entity for this invoice is the US HQ (EIN and billing address), we can reclassify and issue a credit for the VAT portion.

Preliminary reconciliation (provisional):
- Invoice total billed: $4,180.00 (includes VAT $380.00)
- Estimated tokens attributable to long-context streaming experiment (from Ben's sample): ~2.9M tokens
- Estimated tokens attributable to normal traffic: ~500k tokens

I've attached a quick proforma VAT split with options for crediting. Please send:
1) Confirmation of paying legal entity (US HQ vs EU subsidiary) + tax ID or VAT registration details for the EU entity
2) Any contesting evidence for duplicate counts (Ben's team is still validating request IDs)

If you confirm US entity is payer, we will hold VAT portion pending the full log audit and issue a provisional credit within 7 business days.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0147
